info.title: doublegate client gate — loopback HTTP
info.summary: The app, the gate's verbs as JSON-RPC and the MCP binding, on one loopback port.
info.description:
One process on one loopback port, serving four kinds of route: pages that carry no data and need no credential (the app, whose API view renders this document at `/app#/api`); `POST /rpc` (the gate's verbs as JSON-RPC), `POST /mcp` and `GET /openapi.json`, which need a credential — a person's sign-in token or a program's key; two descriptions anyone may read, `GET /identity` and `GET /mcp/catalog.json`; and, while this gate is its own sign-in provider, that provider's five routes.

Generated from the gate's own route table and checked against it on every build, so this document cannot claim something the gate does not do.

**A refusal is not an HTTP error.** `POST /rpc` carries a verb's JSON-RPC refusal inside a `200`. Read the body, not the status line.

**There is no REST mapping of the verbs.** They reach HTTP only through `POST /rpc` as JSON-RPC, verbatim. Do not construct `POST /api/dg/<verb>` or any other `/api/*` path; this gate has no such layer, and its own app calls `/rpc` like every other client.

**A receipt is not an admission.** `dg.ingest` (`doublegate.remember` over MCP) answers with the claim's id and says it is held; nobody else can read it until a reviewer who did not write it promotes it.

**The role is the permission.** Every verb names the least role it needs: reader, agent, reviewer or admin. The account that runs the gate is `admin` on its local socket, any other local account is `agent`, and a credential carries the role this gate gave the person or the key. There is no separate console password.

post.summary: Exchange a code with its PKCE verifier, rotate a refresh token, or exchange a console session for an answer ticket.
post.description: Answers `{access_token, id_token, token_type: Bearer, expires_in: 3600}` and sets the refresh token as the `dg_refresh` cookie (HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/oauth/token). The access token is an EdDSA JWT signed by the deployment key (iss = this issuer, aud = the client id, one hour); the refresh token is opaque, thirty days, rotated on every use, read from the cookie or the `refresh_token` field. A refresh grant that presents neither answers `{session: false}` and sets nothing. While the gate names an answer origin, the token exchange takes the console's own unexpired access token as `subject_token` (type `urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token`) and `resource` that origin exactly, and answers `{access_token, issued_token_type, token_type: Bearer, expires_in: 300}`: a ticket whose aud is the answer origin, which `/rpc` refuses; an API key is no subject token it takes, an `audience` is `invalid_target` and an `actor_token` `invalid_request`. Errors are RFC 6749 §5.2 and RFC 8693 §2.2.2: `{error, error_description}`. Carries cross-origin headers for a listed app origin.

requestBody.description: application/x-www-form-urlencoded: grant_type=authorization_code with code, code_verifier, client_id, redirect_uri; or grant_type=refresh_token with refresh_token; or grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange with subject_token, subject_token_type, requested_token_type and resource

post.summary: The gate's verbs (dg.*) as JSON-RPC, verbatim, over loopback HTTP.
post.description: Byte for byte the message the gate's local socket reads, handled by the same code. Who is calling is the credential's identity — a person's access token or a program's `dgk_` key — and never anything in the body; what it may do is that identity's role, and a verb above the role is a JSON-RPC refusal inside a 200. There is no REST mapping of the verbs: this endpoint is their whole HTTP surface. Each verb's parameters are in components.schemas, and `dg.describe` lists the verbs with the role each needs. Answers the browser's `OPTIONS` preflight, with cross-origin headers for the one app origin this gate's configuration lists for this device, and for no other.

x-dg-verbs.summary: The gate's journal as events, in the order it was appended and never by `ts` (ADR-0109 d3), for a program that follows the lifecycle from a cursor it keeps: a peer. Each event names its type in the journal's own word, the row, replacement group, work area or space it is about, its space and work area, the state it leaves and enters when it moved one, who acted, and the fields `doublegate_sdk.events.CATALOG` lists for its type: identifiers, closed words and counts, never content, a title, a finding, a score or words a person wrote. One call reads at most 1000 events, served or not, and answers `next`, where the next call reads on, and `caught_up`, whether the caller has caught up with what it may read: true when nothing more it would be served lies before the end the read moves toward (the tip, or backward the journal's head), so there is nothing more to read now, and false when the caller reads on, an empty page included. A page full at `limit` reads on, serving nothing, to the next event it would serve, and `next` stands before that event, so a full page says nothing about events the caller may not read; a call that spends its 1000 events first answers false (GAPS 158). Every cursor is sealed (ADR-0117 d4, GAPS 158): encrypted and authenticated under a key derived from the deployment key, one length, and fresh on every answer, so none says where it stands or whether the journal moved, and two are never compared. Below the reviewer role a caller sees every event of a row it wrote and a row's events from its promotion on, a work area's where `dg.lineage` shows it, a group's when it may see every row the group names, and the space registry's; from reviewer up, every served event (AUTH-4). Events that belong to no space, and a pinned authority's, are not served (GAPS 118, 119). Pull only: the gate opens no connection and keeps no position for a reader. Every answer names `tip`, the cursor past the last journal event its projections hold, where a follower starts reading forward from the newest event; `direction: backward` reads from since, or from the tip, toward the journal's head, newest first, and its `next` continues backward (ADR-0111 d2, GAPS 127).
x-dg-verbs.returns: object: {events[{type, object, artifact_id, space, workarea, leaves, enters, by, event_id, ts, trust_class?, content_type?, provisional?, …the type's own fields}], next, tip, caught_up, format_version} — next and tip sealed, caught_up a boolean

The list is applied under one journal lock and refused whole if any entry is refused, one `space-grant-issued` or `-revoked` per entry that changes something; an entry already as asked answers `changed: false` and journals nothing. A connection between two crews is the `read` grants on one crew's space held by the other's keys, made and undone as one such list (ADR-0121 d8); access is never transitive. A revocation deletes nothing and applies to every answer after its event. An admin holds every capability by role and needs no grant (d15).

x-dg-verbs.summary: The open grants, one row per principal and space, each capability with the event that issued it and its reason (`upgrade` for the grants upgrade, ADR-0115 d14); `principal` and `space` narrow the list. A `uid:` principal covers every process that user runs (d17).

x-dg-verbs.summary: The constellation: every artifact as a node, every relation edge, every pin, every ban — the ADR-0035 projection serialized at once, bounded. `label` and `source_uri` are carried only for ACTIVE / SUPERSEDED rows (INV-SEC-10): a held artifact is its existence, never its content. `revision` is the journal tip, and below the reviewer role a digest of the answer itself, which moves only when what the caller is shown moves (GAPS 158); pass it back as `if_revision` and an unchanged graph answers {revision, unchanged: true}. With `workarea` named it is that area's work graph (ADR-0107 d5): the area's rows the caller may see — every row for a reviewer, the promoted rows and the caller's own below (AUTH-4) — plus every row one relation edge away under the same rule, each node marked with its workarea, producer, kind and whether it is foreign to the area, and `completed`, the completion markers. Computed per call, kept nowhere.

Writes nothing, ranks nothing.

post.summary: The client tier's MCP surface: the stateless request/response subset.
post.description: Needs a credential, like `/rpc`: a harness presents the key this gate issued, and its tools act as that program. Origin is validated before the body is read (the spec's DNS-rebinding MUST). No Mcp-Session-Id is ever issued; one that arrives is ignored.

initialize.summary: handshake, the pre-2026 method every shipped SDK still opens with

notification.summary: a notification — answered 202 with no body

202.description: a notification or a client response: no body (spec MUST)

401.description: no credential, or one the gate refuses: {"error":"<kind>: <why>","kind":"missing|malformed|expired|issuer|audience|signature|unavailable|unsupported"}

413.description: the request is larger than this gate accepts (4 MiB unless its configuration says otherwise). Not observed in tests: the gate refuses before reading the body, which a client sees as a reset connection rather than a status line.

get.summary: No SSE stream is offered on this binding.
get.description: 405 by design: the streaming half of Streamable HTTP is not offered, so a client must not open a GET stream and wait.

bearer.description: A person's access token from the sign-in provider this gate names (an OpenID Connect JWT; `GET /identity` says which), or a program's `dgk_…` key this gate issued. Either resolves to one identity with one role, and every verb is held to that role.

error.description: a transport-level refusal from the listener itself

Error.description: The listener's own refusal shape (401/404/413/500/502). A *domain* refusal is not this: it arrives as HTTP 200 carrying RpcErrorEnvelope.

RpcErrorEnvelope.description: A JSON-RPC refusal carried inside a 200 by POST /rpc. Read the body, not the status line.

code.description: -32700 parse error — the body is not JSON; -32600 invalid request — not a JSON-RPC 2.0 object; -32601 method not found; -32602 invalid params, or a refusal carrying its reason; a field the verb does not declare is refused by name; -32603 internal error — the /rpc frame's own guard; the listener survives; -32000 the caller's identity could not be established; -32001 request too large; -32006 the place where new claims are held is full; data.retry_after_ms says when to try again, and below the reviewer role the refusal says nothing of how many claims are held; -32009 writer or source under an operator-signed ban

id.description: omit or null for a notification; /rpc still answers 200 with the response object

params.description: closed per verb: a field the verb does not declare is refused by name. `null` values are refused — omit the field.

JsonRpcResponse.description: Exactly one of result or error. Both arrive with HTTP 200; a JSON-RPC error is not an HTTP error.

RetrievalPaths.description: Which retrieval path answered, and with what. A named degradation ('keyword-only …') is reported here rather than silently producing thinner results.

queues.description: depth per lifecycle state; a depth is what is waiting, never evidence of processing

degraded.description: named degradations in force; empty when none

countersigner.description: the id of the second, independent gate pinned to countersign here, or null when none is pinned

StatusPayload.description: dg.status for this gate, plus what the app's banners are drawn from.

held_steering.description: every held steering row the caller reads, oldest wait first, at most 50, never counted in cap, items or held_back

artifact_id.description: bare sha256 hex on this surface; the MCP surface prefixes it `sha256:`

self_authored.description: the caller wrote this claim, so the gate refuses their signature: the reviewer is never the author

decisions.description: the affirmative verdicts dg.sign accepts from this state; reject is its own verb

attachments.description: the claim's attachment entries, names masked, never a byte

who_can_sign.description: dg.who_can_sign's answer for the row: people by name to an admin and by letter to anyone else, graders, enough, words, notify

RunSnapshot.description: Review-run processing state. `reported: false` means this worker emits no run events — queue depth is not evidence of processing and is not substituted for one.

artifact_id.description: bare sha256 hex on this surface; the MCP surface prefixes it `sha256:`

ratified.description: false on the caller's own claims that are still held, unreviewed

Challenge.description: A nonce for the operator key to sign. Worthless without the private key.

drift.description: each field whose effective value differs from the configured one; empty when the file and this process agree

SettingsPayload.description: Configured (on disk) beside effective (in this process), plus the drift between them. `secrets` reports presence only — never a value.

SettingsValues.description: The draft tables to validate or save.

artifact_id.description: bare sha256 hex on this surface; the MCP surface prefixes it `sha256:`
